* v/e are’ignorant; we know still much Jefs of the soul; but of the effence or nature of God,' we know nothing: it is the prerogative of the Supreme Being alone to comprehend his -own effence.: all the efforts that we can make to attain that knowledge, are arrQgant and ineffectual; it is foreign to the mature of a limited ipiri.t : b.ut our destiny is that of a man, and our desires are those of a God. In a word, man appeals to be Formed to adore, but not to comprehend, the Supreme Being.

II. We may say, however, with Virgil, Jovis omnia plena ; God manifests his exist ence, not only to the internal sensations of our minds, but in every objed' that surrounds

* us in the whole frame of nature; and if we cannot comprehend the Supreme Being by our senses, we may discover his attributes by our reason, almost as clearly as we didinguifh the properties of matter, and many other objeds: and this knowledge is sufficient for us. The end of every other science is some temporal happiness; theology alone proposes an eternal felicity: its objed therefore differs from all other sciences, as the age of threescore and ten differs from eternity. We cannot wonder therefore, that all the inhabitants of the earth, from the time of the creation, have made it their principal sludy, and have exerted all their abilities in the cultivation of it: we ought much rather to be adoniffied that if does not yet more strongly engage the attention of mankind ; and that while they labour so assiduously to acquire those sciences, whose utility extends to so (ho st a space of time, they should so frequently negled that object which can secure their felicity in a future, certain, and eternal evidence. : -

From the first knowledge that we have of the world, that is to say, for about, five thousand years pad, men have blindly searched after the idea of the true God; and by the: weakness of their discernment, they have fallen into a thou fand errors. Paganism at first covered the whole earth, ex cept that family alone which became the dock df the Jewish people: this paganism among different nations had different mixtures of idolatry. Mofes first made known to the Hebrews the true God, and prescribed them his worship: his religion, however, was not adopted by any other people, not even by their neighbours. Jeius Christ appeared upon the earth, abolished a part of the Judaic law, reformed the religion of Mofes, taught His divine .dodrines, and offered

himself as a sacrifice for the salvation of mankind His gospel made a happy progress over all Europe, that is, over the then known part of the earth.- Some time after, Mahomet arose in the ead and preached a religion that he had compounded of the Jewish and Chridian, and of his own ideas.
